# Marking one term two different ways

`makeindex` rejects two marks that share an index key and a printed page but
carry different encapsulations, and Quarto turns that rejection into a failed
render. Page numbers do not exist when the filter runs, so it cannot prevent
the clash — it reports it, once per key. This fixture holds one instance of
each shape that clashes, and one that does not.

A plain mark on [kappa]{.index} against a cross-reference on
[kappa]{.index see="Elsewhere"}.

A `see=` on [lambda]{.index see="Here"} against a `see-also=` on
[lambda]{.index see-also="There"}.

Two marks that agree, which `makeindex` folds together and which must NOT be
reported: [mu]{.index see="Same"} and [mu]{.index see="Same"}.

A term marked plainly twice, which is the ordinary case and must not be
reported either: [nu]{.index} and [nu]{.index}.
